UI copy in English, sentence case.

Read app/player.tsx, app/music-prefs.ts (and its test), app/styles/player.css, app/tokens.css first and follow their patterns.

1. core/ambience.ts (pure). Types for an ambience (id, label, levels) and a level (id, label, color hex, sources: list of {src, type}, gainDb). Export AMBIENCES with one entry, rain, levels in cycle order: off (no sources), drizzle, moderate, storm, with srcs `/ambience/v1/rain-<level>.webm` (type `audio/webm; codecs=opus`) then `.m4a` (type `audio/mp4`), gainDb 0. Export `nextLevel(ambience, levelId)` (off -> drizzle -> moderate -> storm -> off; unknown id -> drizzle), `ambienceLabel(ambience, levelId)` returning e.g. "Rain: drizzle", DEFAULT_AMBIENCE_VOLUME = 0.4, FADE_IN_SEC = 1.5, FADE_OUT_SEC = 1.2, CROSSFADE_SEC = 2, MUTE_FADE_SEC = 0.3, `ambienceGain(volume, muted, gainDb)` (0 when muted, else clamped volume times dB factor), and `parseAmbiencePrefs(value: unknown)` that returns {level, volume} with defaults {off, 0.4} for anything invalid. Unit tests in core/ambience.test.ts.

2. app/ambience-prefs.ts: loadAmbiencePrefs/saveAmbiencePrefs under localStorage key `lectoria.ambience.v1`, guarded like music-prefs (no throw when storage is missing or full). Test like music-prefs.test.ts.

3. app/ambience-controller.ts: class AmbienceController built on an injected engine interface:
   - engine.load(sources) -> Promise<handle> (the engine picks the playable source and decodes it; cache by src),
   - engine.start(handle, gain, fadeSec) -> voice, voice.ramp(gain, sec), voice.stop(fadeSec),
   - engine.unlock() -> Promise<void> (resumes the AudioContext; must be called from a user gesture).
   Controller API: setLevel(id), setVolume(v), setMuted(m), unlock(), dispose(). Rules: switching from off fades in over FADE_IN_SEC; switching between two playing levels crossfades (old voice stop(CROSSFADE_SEC) while the new one starts at 0 and ramps up over CROSSFADE_SEC); switching to off stops with FADE_OUT_SEC; volume changes ramp over 0.1 s; mute and unmute ramp over MUTE_FADE_SEC; while locked (no unlock yet) nothing starts, and the first unlock starts the current level. Async loads must not race: if the level changes while a load is pending, only the latest level may start. Never more than two voices alive. Tests in app/ambience-controller.test.ts with a fake engine: full cycle off->drizzle->moderate->storm->off, crossfade timings, fade in and out, mute silences and unmute restores at the set volume, volume ramp, locked state does not start until unlock, rapid clicks start only the final level, dispose stops everything.

4. app/ambience-engine.ts: real engine with Web Audio. One lazily created AudioContext. load: choose the first source whose type `new Audio().canPlayType(type)` answers "probably" or "maybe", fetch it (same origin), decodeAudioData, cache the promise by src. start: AudioBufferSourceNode with loop = true into a GainNode into destination; fades with setValueAtTime(current) then linearRampToValueAtTime on the audio clock (equal-power is not required here; for the crossfade use setValueCurveAtTime with a sine/cosine curve of 32 points). stop: ramp to 0 then source.stop at the end and disconnect. No test needed beyond a type check.

5. app/rain-button.tsx: client component `RainAmbience({ muted })`. It owns the controller (useRef, created in an effect, disposed on unmount), loads prefs once on mount, saves on change, calls setMuted when the prop changes, and registers one-time `pointerdown` and `keydown` listeners on document that call unlock() (and on the button click itself call unlock() first). It renders a button with className "skip rain" and data-level={level}, aria-label and title from ambienceLabel (e.g. "Rain: storm"), and next to it, only when level is not off, a small range input (0..1 step 0.05, aria-label "Rain volume", class "rain-volume"). Icon is one inline SVG 20x20 viewBox 0 0 20 20, aria-hidden:
   - a cloud path drawn for every level (thin 1.25 stroke). off: outline only, opacity 0.4, no drops, no halo. drizzle: fill #D9DEE3 (light gray), 3 short drop strokes below. moderate: fill #9AA4AE (darker gray), 6 drops. storm: same cloud as moderate, 5 drops plus a small bolt polygon in #F2C230 stroke-less.
   - The halo is a box-shadow ring on the button: drizzle 0 0 0 3px rgba(90,184,240,.35), moderate rgba(242,194,48,.40), storm rgba(229,72,77,.38); border color of the button picks up the level color at 60%.
   - Drops: CSS keyframes translating each drop ~3px down while fading, 1.4 s loop with staggered delays. Bolt: keyframes that keep opacity at 0.85 and flash to 1 with a brief brightness filter for ~120 ms once every ~5 s. Transitions of fill, opacity, box-shadow, border-color: 200 ms ease. Under prefers-reduced-motion: no animation, drops visible and static.
   - CSS goes in a new app/styles/ambience.css imported from app/globals.css after player.css. Use the colors as custom properties declared at the top of that file (--rain-drizzle, --rain-moderate, --rain-storm). Respect dark mode tokens if tokens.css defines them (cloud outline uses currentColor).

6. app/player.tsx: one insertion only, `<RainAmbience muted={muted} />` right after the `.player-volume` label, plus its import. Nothing else in that file changes.

7. Docs: append a short "Rain ambience" paragraph to public/music/README.md pointing to docs/tasks/25-rain-ambience.md and public/ambience/SOURCES.md. Do not edit SOURCES.md or the task doc.

1|# Task 25: rain ambience
2|
3|One rain button next to the music volume. Each click moves to the next
4|level: off, drizzle, moderate, storm, then off again. Each level is its
5|own CC0 loop in `public/ambience/v1/` (see `public/ambience/SOURCES.md`).
6|Only the storm loop has thunder.
7|
8|## Behavior
9|
10|- The rain plays under the music and ignores scene and track changes.
11|- Changing levels crossfades over 2 s with equal-power curves. Turning
12|  rain on fades in over 1.5 s, and turning it off fades out over 1.2 s.
13|- The rain has its own volume (default 0.4). Master mute silences it with
14|  a short fade, and unmute brings it back.
15|- The level and the rain volume persist in localStorage under
16|  `lectoria.ambience.v1` as `{ level, volume }`.
17|- Nothing plays before a user gesture. A level restored from storage
18|  starts on the first pointer or key press anywhere in the page.
19|- Playback uses Web Audio: `AudioBufferSourceNode` with `loop = true`
20|  loops each file with no gap, and `GainNode` ramps run on the audio
21|  clock, so fades still finish in a background tab. The client picks
22|  WebM Opus when `canPlayType` says yes, else M4A.
23|
24|## Button
25|
26|| Level | Label | Icon | Halo |
27||---|---|---|---|
28|| off | Rain: off | Outlined cloud, thin stroke, 40% opacity, no drops | none |
29|| drizzle | Rain: drizzle | Light gray cloud, 3 small drops | celeste `#5AB8F0` |
30|| moderate | Rain: moderate | Darker gray cloud, 6 drops | yellow `#F2C230` |
31|| storm | Rain: storm | Same cloud as moderate, drops and a small bolt | red `#E5484D` |
32|
33|Drops fall in a slow CSS loop, and the bolt flashes briefly every few
34|seconds in storm. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the drops and bolt hold
35|still. State changes crossfade in about 200 ms. The icon is inline SVG.
36|
37|## Code
38|
39|- `core/ambience.ts`, pure: the list of ambiences and their levels
40|  (id, label, color, sources, gain), `nextLevel`, prefs parsing, and the
41|  fade constants. Adding fireplace or wind later means adding one entry.

43|- `app/ambience-controller.ts`: the level, volume, and mute logic against
44|  a small engine interface, so tests use a fake engine.
45|- `app/ambience-engine.ts`: the Web Audio engine.
46|- `app/rain-button.tsx`: the button, its icons, and the rain volume
47|  slider. `app/player.tsx` gains one element next to the volume slider.

1|# Music files
2|
3|The reader fetches `manifest.json` from the client and plays the listed
4|files. Real recordings live in the `lectoria-images` Blob store under
5|`music/v1/<soundtrack>/`, never in this repo. No code change is needed
6|to ship new tracks.
7|
8|## Add or relabel tracks
9|
10|1. Upload the finished file to the store under `music/v1/<soundtrack>/`.
11|   Upload ND-licensed tracks unedited. Every track should play at about
12|   -20 LUFS integrated: either normalize the file, or upload it as is and
13|   set `gainDb` to `-20 - measured LUFS`. Gain above about +1 dB clips
14|   at full volume, so a quiet ND track that needs more is left out.
15|2. Add one `entries` row in `data/music/library.json` with the Blob `src`,
16|   the manifest `soundtrack`, the file `durationSec`, and the credit
17|   fields (`title`, `composer`, `artist`, `license`, `attribution`,
18|   `sourceUrl`, `source`). Set `gainDb` when the file needs a trim and
19|   `noDerivatives: true` for ND tracks, which always play whole.
20|3. Export the etiquetar labels to `data/music/labels.json`.
21|4. Regenerate the manifest:
22|
23|   `npm run build:music data/music/labels.json data/music/library.json --out public/music/manifest.json`
24|
25|   The converter makes one track per labeled segment. It skips discarded
26|   tracks, tracks with no library entry, and rows whose soundtrack style
27|   differs from the export style. It stores `startSec` only when above 0
28|   and `endSec` only when more than 0.5 s before the file end, and it runs
29|   the result through `parseManifest` before writing.
30|
31|## Current library (provisional)
32|
33|Every track in `manifest.json` has `provisional: true`: its labels are
34|the etiquetar.html suggestions, not yet reviewed. `data/music/labels.json`
35|holds those drafts as a schemaVersion 2 export. Replace it with the
36|reviewed export and rerun the converter.
37|
38|- Orchestra: Musopen / Czech National Symphony Orchestra (normalized to
39|  -20 LUFS, 144 kbps), Holst's Mars and Jupiter by the Skidmore College
40|  Orchestra, and 16 Jamendo tracks (as downloaded, `gainDb` trims).
41|- Piano: Jamendo piano tracks that tag as solo piano (as downloaded,
42|  `gainDb` trims).
43|- Just play Chopin: the four Ballades by Frank Lévy, Musopen "Set Chopin
44|  Free" (public domain, CC0), 160 kbps.
45|
46|Left out: the 1923 Columbia acoustic Holst recordings, the USAF Heritage
47|Band wind transcriptions, and the MuseScore render, because they sound
48|out of place next to the orchestras when soundtracks mix.
49|
50|## Track fields

# Git source-control safety

The working tree belongs to the user. Make the change, leave it visible, and
let them decide what becomes history.

## Never without an explicit ask

The user must have asked for that exact write in this session, in their own
words. An explicit request to create a new commit counts anywhere in the user's
own task text, but it is not a request to amend, push, or tag. Finishing a task
without that request does not authorize a history write.

- `commit`, `commit --amend`, `push`, `tag`, `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`,
  `merge`, branch deletion, `reset --hard`, path restore, and `clean -f` all
  require an explicit ask.
- Never publish merely because publication would be useful.

## Before an authorized discard

Recovery is insurance, not authorization. A save never expands what the user
allowed you to delete or overwrite.

When the user explicitly authorized an operation that may discard or broadly
overwrite workspace changes, and the workspace is an ordinary Git checkout:

1. After `muse.read_skill` gives the physical Git skill package path, run:

   ```bash
   bash <git-skill-dir>/scripts/workspace-recovery.sh save before-discard
   ```

2. Keep the printed `refs/tbh/recovery/...` value in your handoff, then perform
   only the exact authorized operation.
3. If the save fails or the workspace is unsupported, stop before destruction
   and ask the user.

To recover that saved tree later, run:

```bash
bash <git-skill-dir>/scripts/workspace-recovery.sh restore <recovery-ref>
```

Restore first saves the current workspace, leaves HEAD, branch, and the real
index in place, and restores the selected snapshot into the worktree. The ref
also retains distinct staged bytes when the same path had later worktree edits.
